A `check-tools` target shall verify that all required host tools (`gcc`, `make`, `avr-gcc`, `avr-nm`) are available before any build step, printing a diagnostic and exiting non-zero if any required tool is absent.

hlr.name: User Manual and Unix Man Page
hlr.text: The project shall provide a user manual (`doc/UserManual.md`) and a Unix man page (`doc/avr-updi-gdb.1`). The man page shall be parseable by the standard `man` utility and shall document the command synopsis, all options, operands, exit codes, and at least one usage example. The `doc/UserManual.md` shall document prerequisites, build instructions, usage, CLI options, and connection wiring for the UPDI adapter.

hlr.name: Distribution Package Bundle
hlr.text: The Makefile shall provide a `bundle` target that produces native distribution packages for three target platforms: a Debian binary package (`dist/avr-updi-gdb_$(VERSION)_amd64.deb`) for Debian/Ubuntu Linux, an RPM binary package (`dist/avr-updi-gdb-$(VERSION)-1.x86_64.rpm`) for Red Hat/Fedora Linux, and a Homebrew formula (`dist/avr-updi-gdb.rb`) for macOS. Each package shall include the `avr-updi-gdb` binary and the man page. All output artefacts shall be written under the `dist/` directory. A `VERSION` variable (defaulting to the value extracted from `git describe`) shall parameterise every package version string.

section.title: Diagnostics and Bring-up
section.intro: Requirements in this section govern operator-facing diagnostic features intended for hardware bring-up and connection troubleshooting. They are activated by explicit CLI flags and never run on the GDB session hot path.

hlr.name: Device-Signature Diagnostic Mode
hlr.text: The server shall provide a one-shot diagnostic mode, activated by the `--device` command-line flag, that opens the UPDI link, reads the target SIGROW (`DEVICEID0..2`, 16-byte `SERNUM`), the SYSCFG.REVID byte, and the UPDI ASI status registers (`ASI_SYS_STATUS`, `ASI_KEY_STATUS`, `ASI_STATUSB`), prints a verbose human-readable report to `stdout`, and exits with status 0 on success or status 1 on any failure. In this mode the `<elf-file>` operand shall be optional, the GDB TCP listener shall not be bound, and no event loop shall be entered. Every failure shall produce a diagnostic on `stderr` that names the failed UPDI step (BREAK, SYNCH, SIGROW read, ASI read) so an operator can distinguish wiring, power, and fuse problems without external instrumentation. `--device` shall be mutually exclusive with `--load`; specifying both shall trigger a usage error and exit status 1.

section.title: Hardware Integration Testing
section.intro: Requirements in this section govern the on-target hardware integration test harness (`tests/hw/hw_test.c`). These tests link against the project's UPDI driver and exercise live AVR-Dx silicon over a serial UPDI link. They are manual-only and are explicitly excluded from `make test` so that unit-test execution remains hardware-independent and CI-safe.

hlr.name: On-Target Hardware Integration Test Harness
hlr.text: The project shall provide a standalone, manual-only on-target hardware integration test harness, separate from the unit-test suite, that validates the UPDI driver, device-info report, SRAM and FLASH memory access, and the GDB RSP server against live AVR-Dx silicon. The harness shall be organised into four opt-in groups: Group A (read-only link and device-info probes), Group B (non-destructive SRAM round-trips with size and address-mode variants), Group C (destructive FLASH erase/write/verify, gated by an explicit confirmation variable), and Group D (RSP server spawn-and-probe over TCP, gated by an opt-in variable). The harness shall be configurable via environment variables and command-line flags (serial port, expected device ID, SRAM probe address, FLASH page address, RSP TCP port, verbosity), and shall accept an explicit `--addr-24bit` switch to validate 24-bit UPDI addressing on parts whose FLASH lies above 64 KiB. The Makefile shall expose dedicated targets `hw-test` (Groups A+B), `hw-test-nvm` (Groups A+B+C), `hw-test-rsp` (Groups A+B+D), and `hw-test-all` (all groups); none of these targets shall ever be invoked by `make test`.

function.title: Introduction
function.name: intro
function.intro: Each LLR ID follows the pattern `LLR-XXX-NN`, where `XXX` is a module code and `NN` is a zero-padded two-digit sequence number. Module codes: `MAIN` (`src/main.c`), `UPDI` (`src/updi.c`), `RSP` (`src/gdb_rsp.c`), `ELF` (`src/elf_parser.c`), `FSM` (`src/fsm_mapper.c`), `MON` (`src/monitor.c`), `INST` (`Makefile`, `doc/avr-updi-gdb.1`, `doc/UserManual.md`), `HWTEST` (`tests/hw/hw_test.c`). IDs are permanent contracts and may not be renumbered or reused once allocated.

function.title: src/main.c — Entry Point and Event Loop
function.name: main
function.intro: Requirements for `main()`, `parse_args()`, and `event_loop()`. These functions own the application lifecycle from argument parsing through resource cleanup.

llr.text: `parse_args()` shall populate an `AppConfig` struct from `argc`/`argv`. If any unrecognised argument is encountered, it shall print a usage message to `stderr` and call `exit(1)`.

When not supplied on the command line, `parse_args()` shall apply the following defaults to the `AppConfig` fields: `gdb_port` = 1234, `baud_rate` = 115200, `load_flash` = false. The `<serial-device>` and `<elf-file>` positional arguments are mandatory; absence of either shall trigger the usage error path.

`main()` shall call `updi_open()` and validate the returned file descriptor before calling `rsp_listen()`. A failure from either shall cause `main()` to release any already-open resources and return exit code 1.

When the `--load` flag is set, `main()` shall iterate over all `PT_LOAD` ELF program headers and call `updi_nvm_write_flash()` for each segment whose `p_filesz > 0` and whose virtual address lies below the SRAM base (i.e. flash-resident segments only). Segments with `p_vaddr >= ctx.sram_base` shall be skipped. All qualifying segments shall be written before entering `event_loop()`. A flash write failure shall cause `main()` to print an error to `stderr` and return exit code 1.

`event_loop()` shall multiplex `listen_fd`, `gdb_fd`, and `updi_fd` using a single POSIX `select()` call with no timeout. On each iteration it shall: accept a GDB client on `listen_fd` if `gdb_fd` is -1; forward console bytes from `updi_fd` to `stdout` via `updi_console_poll()`; dispatch RSP packets from `gdb_fd` via `rsp_recv_packet()` and `rsp_dispatch()`. No POSIX threads shall be created.

`main()` shall register a `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` handler that sets the global `volatile sig_atomic_t g_quit` flag to 1. `event_loop()` shall test `g_quit` at the top of each loop iteration and return immediately when the flag is set, without closing any file descriptors itself.

On all exit paths, `main()` shall release resources in this exact order: (1) `rsp_close(cfg.gdb_fd)` if `gdb_fd >= 0`, (2) `rsp_close(cfg.listen_fd)`, (3) `elf_close(&ctx)`, (4) `updi_close(cfg.updi_fd)`. The process shall exit with code 0 on normal termination and code 1 on any fatal initialisation or flash-write failure.

`parse_args()` shall recognise the `--device` long option, set `cfg->device_info = true`, and accept the absence of the `<elf-file>` operand without error. Specifying both `--device` and `--load` on the same command line shall cause `parse_args()` to print `"error: --device is mutually exclusive with --load"` to `stderr`, print the usage synopsis, and call `exit(1)`.

When `cfg.device_info` is true, `main()` shall: (1) call `updi_open()`; (2) on success call `updi_read_device_info()`; (3) on success format and print to `stdout` a multi-line report containing `Serial device:`, `Baud rate:`, `Signature:` (3 hex bytes), `Family:` (looked up via a static `device_family[]` table indexed by signature \u2014 unknown signatures shall print `unknown device`), `Revision:`, `Serial:` (10 hex bytes), and `UPDI status: SYS_STATUS=0x.. KEY_STATUS=0x.. STATUSB=0x..`; (4) call `updi_close()` and return. The function shall **not** call `rsp_listen()`, `elf_find_avros_tables()`, `fsm_build_thread_list()`, or `event_loop()`. On any UPDI failure the function shall print a verbose diagnostic to `stderr` that names the failed step (e.g. `"updi-open"`, `"sigrow"`, `"sys-status"`) and return exit code 1.

function.title: src/updi.c — UPDI Physical Layer
function.name: updi
function.intro: Requirements for all public functions in `src/updi.c`: link initialisation, memory access, execution control, NVM programming, and console bridging.

llr.text: `updi_open()` shall open the UART device and configure it for 8E2 framing (8 data bits, even parity, 2 stop bits) in raw half-duplex mode using `termios`. `cfmakeraw()`, `CS8`, `CSTOPB`, `PARENB` (with `PARODD` cleared), and explicit baud setting via `cfsetispeed()`/`cfsetospeed()` shall be applied. If `tcsetattr()` returns `EINVAL` when setting `PARENB` (Linux PTY slaves strip parity from virtual terminals), the function shall retry with `PARENB` cleared so the link still works against PTY-backed test harnesses. The function shall return the open file descriptor on success or -1 on failure.

`updi_open()` shall execute up to three cold-start attempts. Attempt 0 (fast path) shall write a single 0x00 wake byte at the configured session baud rate, followed by `tcdrain()` and `tcflush(fd, TCIFLUSH)` to discard the half-duplex echo. Attempts 1 and 2 (slow path) shall instead generate a multi-millisecond line-low pulse by temporarily switching the kernel baud rate to 300 baud with `CSTOPB` cleared (1 stop bit) via `tcsetattr(TCSADRAIN)`, then writing two 0x00 bytes each followed immediately by `tcdrain()` to guarantee the byte is actually clocked out of the UART FIFO before the next operation. Each byte at 300 baud holds the TX line low for ≈33 ms (≥60 ms total — sufficient to reset the target's UPDI clock and contention detector on a cold power-on with passive single-wire combiners), and the half-duplex echoes are read-and-discarded at 300 baud. After both BREAK bytes, `updi_open()` shall sleep ≈50 ms (`nanosleep()`) so that any echo bytes still in flight on the line bus reach the kernel RX queue at 300-baud framing, then `tcflush(TCIFLUSH)` discards them. Only then shall the session baud rate be restored (`tcsetattr(TCSADRAIN)` followed by a second `tcflush(TCIFLUSH)`). Without `tcdrain()` after each write, the subsequent baud switch flushes or re-clocks the queued BREAK byte, destroying the line-low pulse; without the 50 ms settle, late echo bytes arrive AFTER the baud restore, get framed at 115200 baud, and desynchronise every subsequent frame echo. This mirrors avrdude's `serialupdi` programmer exactly (verified by `strace`) and is necessary because no portable POSIX API generates a multi-ms BREAK on demand — `tcsendbreak()` is too short and not honoured by all kernel UART drivers (notably the RPi PL011).

After the wake byte (attempt 0) or 300-baud double-break (attempts 1–2), `updi_open()` shall transmit `STCS ASI_CTRLB = ASI_CTRLB_CCDETDIS` (0x08) to disable the target's collision/contention detector, then `STCS ASI_CTRLA = ASI_CTRLA_IBDLY` (0x80) to enable inter-byte delay on the target's responses, then probe the link with `LDCS ASI_STATUSA` (opcode `0x80 | 0x00 = 0x80`). `ASI_STATUSA` carries UPDIREV in its upper nibble and is always readable while UPDI is enabled, including before any reset. If any STCS write or the LDCS probe fails, `updi_open()` shall advance to the next attempt. After 3 consecutive failed attempts the function shall return -1 and the caller shall treat the link as unavailable.

`updi_mem_read()` and `updi_mem_write()` shall transfer up to `UPDI_MAX_BLOCK` (256) bytes per UPDI burst using a three-frame sequence per datasheet §35.3.3.4: (1) a pointer-set frame — `ST_PTR_WORD` (`0x69`) followed by the 16-bit target address in little-endian order when `addr ≤ 0xFFFF`, or `ST_PTR_LONG` (`0x6A`) followed by the 24-bit address in little-endian order when `addr > 0xFFFF` — with a single ACK readback; (2) `REPEAT` (`0xA0`) followed by `(block_len - 1)`; (3) `LD ptr++` (`0x24`) for reads or `ST ptr++` (`0x64`) for writes. The selection between the 16-bit and 24-bit pointer-set forms shall be automatic based on the requested address, with the 24-bit form required for access to the AVR128DA/DB mapped-Flash region above 64 KiB. If `len` exceeds `UPDI_MAX_BLOCK`, the function shall split the request into consecutive bursts automatically, with no size restriction imposed on the caller.

`updi_mem_read()` shall use `select()` with a 100 ms timeout before each `read()` call on the UART file descriptor to enforce a per-byte inactivity deadline. If `select()` returns zero (timeout) before a byte is available, the function shall abandon the current transaction and return -1.
`updi_mem_write()` shall write arbitrary byte ranges to the SRAM address space of the target using UPDI ST commands and return 0 on success or -1 on UART framing error, timeout, or UPDI NAK.

`updi_nvm_write_flash()` shall require `word_addr` to be aligned to a 512-byte FLASH page boundary and `len` to be a non-zero multiple of 512. It shall enter NVM programming mode by transmitting the `KEY` opcode (`0xE0`) with the 8-byte string `"NVMProg "`, asserting reset with `STCS ASI_RESET_REQ = 0x59`, releasing reset with `STCS ASI_RESET_REQ = 0x00`, then polling `ASI_SYS_STATUS` via LDCS for bit 3 (NVMPROG, mask `0x08`) up to 100 iterations (≈ 100 ms). For each page it shall write the page data via `updi_mem_write()`, write `0x03` (ERWP) to `NVMCTRL_CTRLA`, and poll `NVMCTRL_STATUS` bit 0 (BUSY) clear up to 20 iterations (≈ 20 ms). On exit it shall toggle `ASI_RESET_REQ` `0x59` then `0x00` to release the target. Timeout of either poll shall return -1; a `NVMCTRL_STATUS` WRERR (bit 2) shall return `UPDI_ERR_WP`.

`updi_halt()` is a Phase 2 stub. It shall return -1 unconditionally with no UART traffic. The full halt sequence (OCD register manipulation, STOPPED-bit polling) is part of the AVR On-Chip Debug specification and is implemented by the Phase 3 OCD layer.
`updi_step()` is a Phase 2 stub. It shall return -1 unconditionally with no UART traffic. Single-step is implemented by the Phase 3 OCD layer.
`updi_run()` is a Phase 2 stub. It shall return -1 unconditionally with no UART traffic. CPU resume is implemented by the Phase 3 OCD layer.

`updi_mem_read()` shall be callable while the target CPU is in the RUNNING state (not halted). The function shall not call `updi_halt()` internally, permitting non-intrusive SRAM sampling for the monitor sub-commands and console polling without interrupting firmware execution.

`updi_console_poll()` shall perform a background `updi_mem_read()` of the avrOS software UART output buffer and return any pending bytes to the caller without halting the CPU. The function shall return the number of bytes read (0 if none pending) or -1 on UPDI error.

`updi_read_device_info(fd, info)` shall populate the caller-supplied `UpdiDeviceInfo` struct with: 3 SIGROW DEVICEID bytes from physical address `0x1100`-`0x1102` (datasheet §7.6.1, Table 7-4), the SYSCFG.REVID byte at `0x0F01` (datasheet §8.3.2.1; SYSCFG base `0x0F00`), 16 SERNUM bytes at `0x1110`-`0x111F` (datasheet §7.6.2.3), and the three ASI registers `ASI_SYS_STATUS`, `ASI_KEY_STATUS`, `ASI_STATUSB` read via `LDCS`. The function shall be non-destructive (no halt, no NVM activity). On any UPDI read failure it shall set `info->fail_op` to a short ASCII tag (`"sigrow"`, `"revid"`, `"sernum"`, `"sys-status"`, `"key-status"`, `"asi-statusb"`) and return -1; on success it shall set `info->fail_op = NULL` and return 0.

After each successful `LDCS ASI_STATUSA` link probe inside `updi_open()`, the function shall read the target's 32-byte System Information Block by transmitting `SYNCH` (`0x55`) followed by opcode `UPDI_OP_KEY_SIB` (`0xE6`) and reading exactly `UPDI_SIB_LEN` (32) bytes of response — looped over `read()` until the full block is collected. The SIB read serves two purposes: (1) it confirms the link end-to-end (target must be actively responding to return non-echo bytes), and (2) it wakes a target that was left in UPDI SLEEP from a prior debug session. Without this step a sleeping target will appear to accept every link-layer probe (STCS, LDCS) — those frames merely echo on the half-duplex line — yet reject every memory access, manifesting as `updi_mem_read()` returning -1 immediately after a successful `updi_open()`. avrdude's `serialupdi` issues this exact 32-byte SIB read on every connect; the response payload (e.g. `" AVR P:2D:1-3M2 (A7.KV001.0)\0"`) is discarded by `updi_open()` since the caller currently only needs the wake side-effect. If the SIB read times out or returns fewer than 32 bytes the attempt shall be abandoned and the next cold-start attempt shall begin.

function.title: src/gdb_rsp.c — GDB Remote Serial Protocol Server
function.name: rsp
function.intro: Requirements for RSP packet framing, dispatch, GDB packet handlers, session lifecycle, and socket configuration.

llr.text: `rsp_listen()` shall set `SO_REUSEADDR` on the listener socket before calling `bind()`. After `rsp_accept()` returns a connected client socket, the client socket shall have `TCP_NODELAY` set to disable Nagle's algorithm.

`rsp_recv_packet()` shall scan incoming bytes discarding pre-packet ACK/NAK characters until a `$` delimiter is received. It shall accumulate the payload with a running XOR checksum until `#` is received, then compare the computed checksum against the two ASCII-hex checksum bytes that follow. On match it shall write `+` to the socket and return the payload length; on mismatch it shall write `-` and return -1.

The `on_read_regs` handler for the `g` packet shall delegate to `fsm_get_registers()` for the currently selected virtual thread (stored in `RspContext.g_thread_p`, defaulting to the active FSM thread when zero or negative) and return the resulting 78-character hex string. The FSM mapper is responsible for placing R0-R31 at hex positions 0-63, SREG at 64-65, SPL at 66-67, SPH at 68-69, and PC as 4-byte little-endian at positions 70-77; live SREG/SP bytes for the active thread are read via `updi_mem_read()` from within `fsm_get_registers()`.

The `on_write_regs` handler for the `G` packet and the single-register `P` handler shall write the supplied register values to the target's CPU register file via `updi_mem_write()` and return `OK` on success or an error reply on UPDI failure.

The `on_read_mem` handler for `m addr,len` shall call `updi_mem_read()` with the decoded address and length, and return the result as a hex string. Both FLASH and SRAM addresses shall be accepted; address-space routing is handled by `updi_mem_read()` based on the raw address value.

The `on_write_mem` handler for `M addr,len:data` (hex-encoded) and `X addr,len:data` (binary-encoded) packets shall call `updi_mem_write()` for SRAM addresses and `updi_nvm_write_flash()` for FLASH addresses, returning `OK` on success or an error reply on failure.

The `on_insert_bp` handler for `Z0 addr,kind` shall: (1) check the breakpoint table for an existing entry at the requested address; if not present, (2) read and save the 2-byte instruction word via `updi_mem_read()`, (3) write the AVR BREAK opcode (0x9598) via `updi_nvm_write_flash()`, and (4) return `OK`. A duplicate insert shall return `OK` without a second flash write.

The `on_remove_bp` handler for `z0 addr,kind` shall look up the requested address in the breakpoint table, restore the saved 2-byte instruction word via `updi_nvm_write_flash()`, remove the entry from the table, and return `OK`. If the address is not in the table, the handler shall return an error reply.
When `on_insert_bp` is called and all `RSP_MAX_BREAKPOINTS` (16) breakpoint table slots are occupied, it shall not write to FLASH and shall return the GDB error reply `E08`.
The `on_step` handler for `s`/`vCont;s` shall call `updi_step()` and, on success, send a stop-reason packet of the form `T05thread:<active_thread_id>;` to the GDB client.

The `on_continue` handler for `c`/`vCont;c` shall call `updi_run()` followed by `fsm_invalidate()`, then poll by calling `updi_halt()` until the CPU stops. On halt, it shall call `fsm_build_thread_list()` to rebuild the thread list and send a stop-reason packet to the GDB client.

`rsp_dispatch()` shall handle the following packets inline without invoking any `RspHandlers` slot, because each response is a fixed string requiring no target interaction: `qSupported` (responds with `PacketSize=800;QStartNoAckMode+;multiprocess-;vContSupported+`), `qAttached` (responds `1`), `QStartNoAckMode` (calls `rsp_set_noack(true)` and responds `OK`), and `vCont?` (responds `vCont;c;s`).

The `on_detach` handler for the `D` packet shall call `updi_run()` to resume the target, close the GDB client socket, reset `cfg->gdb_fd` to -1, and allow the event loop to re-enter the listening state. The server process shall not exit.
The `on_detach` handler for the `k` (kill) packet shall set `g_quit = 1` to cause the event loop to exit, triggering the full resource teardown sequence defined by LLR-MAIN-07.

The `on_monitor` handler for `qRcmd` shall pass the raw ASCII-hex-encoded command body directly to `monitor_dispatch()` without pre-decoding it, and relay the return code to the GDB client as `OK` on success (return 0), an O-packet error message on UPDI failure (return -1), or an empty reply on unrecognised sub-command (return -2).

The `H` (set-thread) packet handler shall store the requested GDB thread ID in the session context and use it to select the virtual thread for subsequent `g`/`G`/`P` register operations. Thread ID -1 (all threads) and 0 (any thread) shall both be interpreted as selecting the active FSM thread.

`elf_open()` shall read the first 16 bytes of the ELF binary and verify: the 4-byte magic sequence (0x7F `'E'` `'L'` `'F'`), `EI_CLASS == ELFCLASS32`, and `e_machine == EM_AVR` (0x0053). Any validation failure shall cause `elf_open()` to log a warning and return -1 without any heap allocation.

`elf_open()` shall locate the `.symtab` section (type `SHT_SYMTAB`) and its associated string table section (index given by `sh_link`), and load both into heap-allocated buffers stored in `ctx->symtab` and `ctx->strtab`. `ctx->sym_count` and `ctx->strtab_size` shall be set accordingly. On any `malloc` failure, `elf_open()` shall free all partial allocations and return -1.

`elf_find_avros_tables()` shall perform a single O(sym_count) linear scan of `ctx->symtab`, compare each symbol name against the 8 avrOS sentinel names defined in SDD §6.3.3, and populate the corresponding fields of `AvrOsSymbolIndex` for each match. The function shall return 0 (success, even if partial) or -1 only on an internal ELF read error.

`elf_flash_addr()` shall convert an ELF virtual memory address to a physical FLASH word address using the formula: `physical_word_addr = (vma - ctx->flash_base) / 2`. All FLASH-resident avrOS symbol addresses stored in `AvrOsSymbolIndex` shall be computed via this function.

When `elf_find_avros_tables()` completes the symbol scan and fewer than the expected avrOS symbols were found, it shall return 0 (not -1). Fields of `AvrOsSymbolIndex` for absent symbols shall retain their zero-initialised values, and the function shall log an informational message identifying which symbols were not found.

`elf_close()` shall free `ctx->symtab`, free `ctx->strtab`, and close `ctx->fd`. After returning, `ctx->symtab` and `ctx->strtab` shall be set to NULL and `ctx->fd` to -1. `elf_close()` shall be safe to call on a partially initialised `ElfContext` (e.g., after a failed `elf_open()`).

`src/elf_parser.c` shall obtain ELF32 type definitions via a platform-conditional include: on Linux (`#ifdef __linux__`) it shall use the system header `<elf.h>`; on all other platforms it shall include the bundled portability shim `src/elf.h`. The shim shall define at minimum: `Elf32_Half`, `Elf32_Word`, `Elf32_Off`, `Elf32_Addr`, `Elf32_Ehdr`, `Elf32_Phdr`, `Elf32_Shdr`, `Elf32_Sym`, the `ELFMAG`/`SELFMAG` magic constants, `EI_CLASS`, `ELFCLASS32`, `EM_AVR` (0x0053), `PT_LOAD`, `SHT_SYMTAB`, `SHT_STRTAB`, `SHN_UNDEF`, and the `ELF32_ST_BIND`/`ELF32_ST_TYPE` accessor macros.

`elf_open()` shall iterate over all ELF program headers and identify `PT_LOAD` segments. The first `PT_LOAD` segment encountered shall be treated as the FLASH load segment: its `p_vaddr` and `p_filesz` shall be stored in `ctx->flash_base` and `ctx->flash_size` respectively. The second `PT_LOAD` segment shall be treated as the SRAM load segment: its `p_vaddr` and `p_memsz` shall be stored in `ctx->sram_base` and `ctx->sram_size` respectively. If fewer than two `PT_LOAD` segments are present the absent values shall remain zero. These fields are the sole inputs to `elf_flash_addr()`.

`fsm_build_thread_list()` shall read `idx->fsm_table_count` consecutive 9-byte `fsmStateMachineDescr_t` records from the FLASH address `idx->fsm_table_addr` via `updi_mem_read()`. Each descriptor carries a 2-byte `name` pointer (FLASH), a 2-byte `stateMachine` pointer (SRAM, or NULL for an initializer slot that shall be skipped), a 2-byte `handler` function pointer, a 1-byte `priority`, and a 2-byte `instance`. For each non-NULL `stateMachine` pointer, the function shall read 2 bytes from `stateMachine + 9` (the `currState` field of `fsmStateMachine_t`) to obtain the current state function pointer and store it in `thread->state_fn`. A UPDI read failure at any point shall cause the function to return -1.

`fsm_build_thread_list()` shall assign `thread->gdb_id = loop_index + 1` (1-based) to each FSM entry in the order the entries appear in the FLASH table. Thread IDs shall not be reassigned within a debug session, ensuring the same FSM always maps to the same GDB thread ID.

`fsm_build_thread_list()` shall read the 2-byte SRAM value at `idx->current_fsm_addr` (avrOS `currStateMachine`) and compare it against each retained FSM entry's `stateMachine` pointer. The matching entry shall have `thread->is_active = true` and its `gdb_id` stored in `ctx->active_id`. If no entry matches, `ctx->active_id` shall be set to 0.

`fsm_get_registers()` shall set the PC field (GDB register index 35, 4-byte little-endian at hex positions 70–77 of the 78-character g-packet buffer) to `thread->state_fn`. For non-active threads, R0–R31 (indices 0–31) and SREG (index 32) shall be zero-filled, and SPL (index 33) and SPH (index 34) shall be set to zero. For the active thread, SREG (index 32, hex positions 64–65), SPL (index 33, hex positions 66–67), and SPH (index 34, hex positions 68–69) shall be read from the target SRAM via `updi_mem_read()`.

`fsm_build_thread_list()` shall process at most `FSM_MAX_THREADS` (32) entries from the FSM registration table regardless of `idx->fsm_table_count`. If `idx->fsm_table_count` exceeds `FSM_MAX_THREADS`, the function shall log a diagnostic warning and return `FSM_MAX_THREADS` as the thread count without returning an error to the GDB client.

`fsm_get_registers()` shall not issue any UPDI memory read targeting a non-active thread's stack region. The suspended FSM register frame shall be constructed entirely from the cached `thread->state_fn` value; the SP field shall be zeroed for non-active threads.

function.title: src/monitor.c — avrOS System Introspection
function.name: monitor
function.intro: Requirements for `monitor_dispatch()` and its static sub-command helpers `cmd_events()` and `cmd_queues()`.

llr.text: `monitor_dispatch()` shall hex-decode the ASCII-hex-encoded `cmd` string (pairs of hex digit characters) into a plain-text command string before any prefix or sub-command matching is attempted. An odd-length or invalid hex-digit sequence shall be treated as an unrecognised command.

`monitor_dispatch()` shall verify that the decoded command string begins with the prefix `"avros "` (case-sensitive, including the trailing space). If the prefix does not match, the function shall send a usage-hint O-packet to the GDB console and return -2.

`cmd_events()` shall call `updi_mem_read()` to read `idx->event_count` consecutive 4-byte `evntDescriptor_t` records from FLASH at `idx->event_table_addr`. For each descriptor it shall dereference the `name` pointer (FLASH) to read the event's NUL-terminated display name (up to 31 chars) and the `status` pointer (SRAM) to read the 1-byte status flag, then append a line of the form `" <name>: <status>\n"` and send the complete buffer as RSP O-packets.

`cmd_queues()` shall call `updi_mem_read()` to read `idx->queue_count` consecutive 10-byte `queDescriptor_t` records from FLASH at `idx->queue_table_addr`. For each descriptor it shall extract and format the `capacity` and `sizeOfElement` fields as a one-line entry and send the complete table as RSP O-packets.

All monitor output shall be assembled into a temporary buffer of at most 512 bytes, hex-encoded (each ASCII byte converted to 2 hex characters per RSP O-packet spec), and transmitted to the GDB client as one or more RSP O-packets via `rsp_send_packet()`.

`monitor_dispatch()` and all of its static helpers (`cmd_events()`, `cmd_queues()`) shall use `updi_mem_read()` exclusively for all target memory access. None of these functions shall call `updi_halt()`, ensuring that monitor commands never interrupt firmware execution.

function.title: Makefile and Documentation
function.name: inst
function.intro: Requirements for the Makefile installation targets (`install`, `uninstall`, `check-tools`, `bundle`) and the documentation deliverables (`doc/UserManual.md`, `doc/avr-updi-gdb.1`). Bundle artefacts are written to `dist/`.

llr.text: The Makefile shall provide a `check-tools` target that tests for the presence of every required host tool: `gcc` (or `cc`), `make`, `avr-gcc`, and `avr-nm`. For each absent tool the target shall print a diagnostic message to `stderr` naming the missing tool and then exit with status 1. The target shall exit with status 0 only when all required tools are found.

The Makefile `install` target shall accept a `PREFIX` variable (default `/usr/local`) and install: the compiled `avr-updi-gdb` binary to `$(PREFIX)/bin/avr-updi-gdb` and the man page `doc/avr-updi-gdb.1` to `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1/avr-updi-gdb.1`. The target shall create any missing intermediate directories using `install -d`. The binary shall be installed with mode 0755 and the man page with mode 0644.

The Makefile `uninstall` target shall remove `$(PREFIX)/bin/avr-updi-gdb` and `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1/avr-updi-gdb.1` using `rm -f`. The target shall be idempotent: running it when the files are already absent shall exit with status 0 without error.

The project shall include a user manual at `doc/UserManual.md` documenting: (1) prerequisites (required host tools and their minimum versions), (2) build instructions (`make`, `make test`), (3) connection wiring for the UPDI adapter (1 kΩ resistor on UPDI pin, serial adapter TX/RX orientation), (4) launch invocation and all CLI options, and (5) at least two complete usage examples (one with `--load`, one without).

trace.name: User Manual and Unix Man Page

llr.text: The project shall include a Unix man page at `doc/avr-updi-gdb.1` in `groff`/`troff` format. The man page shall contain at minimum: NAME, SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS (one entry per CLI flag), OPERANDS, EXIT STATUS, EXAMPLES, and SEE ALSO sections. The man page shall be parseable by `man -l doc/avr-updi-gdb.1` without error or warning on Linux.

trace.name: User Manual and Unix Man Page

llr.text: The Makefile `bundle` target shall produce a Debian binary package at `dist/avr-updi-gdb_$(VERSION)_amd64.deb` using `dpkg-deb --build`. The package staging tree shall install the binary to `usr/bin/avr-updi-gdb` (mode 0755) and the man page to `usr/share/man/man1/avr-updi-gdb.1` (mode 0644). The `DEBIAN/control` file shall declare at minimum: `Package: avr-updi-gdb`, `Version`, `Architecture: amd64`, `Maintainer`, and `Description` fields.

The Makefile `bundle` target shall produce an RPM binary package at `dist/avr-updi-gdb-$(VERSION)-1.x86_64.rpm` using `rpmbuild`. A `.spec` file shall be generated in the build tree containing at minimum: `Name`, `Version`, `Release: 1`, `Summary`, `License`, `%description`, `%install`, and `%files` sections. The `%files` section shall list `/usr/bin/avr-updi-gdb` and `/usr/share/man/man1/avr-updi-gdb.1`.

The Makefile `bundle` target shall produce a Homebrew formula at `dist/avr-updi-gdb.rb`. The formula shall be a valid Ruby file usable with `brew install --formula dist/avr-updi-gdb.rb`. It shall define at minimum: `desc`, `homepage`, `url`, `sha256`, `version`, `license`, and an `install` block that places the binary using `bin.install` and the man page using `man1.install`.

function.title: tests/hw/hw_test.c — On-Target Hardware Integration Test Harness
function.name: hwtest
function.intro: Requirements for the manual-only on-target hardware integration test program. The harness links against `src/updi.c` (and, for Group D, spawns the production `build/avr-updi-gdb` binary via `fork`/`execl`) and runs against live AVR-Dx silicon connected via a UART/UPDI adapter.

llr.text: `tests/hw/hw_test.c` shall accept its configuration from environment variables and from long-form command-line options. Recognised settings: `HW_PORT` / `--port` (serial device path; default `/dev/ttyUSB0`), `HW_DEVICE_ID` / `--device-id` (expected 24-bit SIGROW signature as a hex literal; default `0x1E970A` for AVR128DA48), `HW_SRAM_ADDR` / `--sram-addr` (16-bit SRAM probe address; default `0x7000`), `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR` / `--flash-page` (FLASH page-aligned address used by Group C; default `0x1FE00`), `HW_RSP_PORT` / `--rsp-port` (TCP port for Group D; default `1234`), `HW_TEST_ELF` / `--elf` (optional ELF binary passed to the spawned RSP server in Group D), `HW_ADDR_24BIT` / `--addr-24bit` (boolean; when true, FLASH access uses the 24-bit UPDI addressing path), and `HW_VERBOSE` / `--verbose` (boolean; enables per-byte tracing). CLI flags shall override the corresponding environment values.

Group A (read-only link probes) shall execute the following ordered checks against the live target: **A1** open the serial port and perform the UPDI cold-start handshake (BREAK + SYNCH); **A2** call `updi_read_device_info()` and capture the result for downstream assertions; **A3** verify that the captured `DEVICEID0..2` bytes match the configured `HW_DEVICE_ID`; **A4** verify that the SIGROW signature is not all-zero and not all-`0xFF`; **A5** verify that `SYSCFG.REVID` is non-zero; **A6** verify that the 10-byte `SERNUM` field is not all-zero and not all-`0xFF`; **A7** verify that `ASI_SYS_STATUS.NVMPROG` is clear (target is not stuck in a programming session). Each individual check shall be reported as a separate `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]` line.

Group B (non-destructive SRAM round-trips) shall execute the following ordered checks at `HW_SRAM_ADDR`: **B0** single-byte write/read; **B1** 64-byte buffer write/read; **B1a** SIGROW read repeated twice and compared (isolates the read path from the write path); **B1b** write 64 bytes of constant `0xAA` then read back (value-independence check); **B1c** write a known pattern once then read it back twice and compare both reads (detects live CPU writes to the probed region — on failure the harness shall hint that the operator pick a different `--sram-addr` / `HW_SRAM_ADDR`); **B2** 600-byte buffer write/read (exercises multi-chunk transfer); **B3** when `HW_ADDR_24BIT` is true, a small write/read at the configured FLASH page address using the 24-bit UPDI addressing path. None of the Group B steps shall modify FLASH.

Group C (destructive FLASH write/verify) shall execute only when the environment variable `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES` is set; otherwise the group shall be reported as skipped. When confirmed, Group C shall perform: **C1** erase the FLASH page at `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR`, then write a deterministic pattern via the NVM controller; **C2** read the page back and verify a byte-for-byte match against the written pattern. The harness shall enter and leave the NVM programming session cleanly (NVMPROG key in, NVMPROG key cleared on exit) so that subsequent Group A/B checks find the target in a non-programming state.

Group D (RSP server spawn-and-probe) shall execute only when the environment variable `HW_TEST_RSP=YES` is set; otherwise the group shall be reported as skipped. When enabled, Group D shall `fork` and `execl` the production `build/avr-updi-gdb` binary with the configured serial port and optional `HW_TEST_ELF`, wait briefly for the server's TCP listener to bind on `HW_RSP_PORT`, then perform: **D1** connect a TCP client to `127.0.0.1:HW_RSP_PORT` and verify the connection is accepted; **D2** send an RSP `qSupported` packet (`$qSupported#37`) and verify a non-empty, properly-framed RSP reply is received. The harness shall terminate the spawned server cleanly (SIGTERM + `waitpid`) on completion or on test failure.

The Makefile shall expose four targets that drive `tests/hw/hw_test.c`: `hw-test` runs Groups A+B (read-only); `hw-test-nvm` runs Groups A+B+C and forwards `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES`; `hw-test-rsp` runs Groups A+B+D and forwards `HW_TEST_RSP=YES`; `hw-test-all` runs all four groups. Every hw-test variable (`HW_PORT`, `HW_DEVICE_ID`, `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR`, `HW_RSP_PORT`, `HW_TEST_ELF`, `HW_ADDR_24BIT`, `HW_VERBOSE`) shall be passed through to the child process via the target recipes. None of these targets shall be a dependency of the default `make test` target or be built by `make all`. The `make help` output shall document each variable, its default, and a brief description.

file.header: Unit tests for `src/main.c`: argument parsing, event loop, signal handling, and resource teardown. Uses `fork()`/`waitpid()` to test `exit()` paths and a mock UPDI/RSP layer to exercise the event loop without real hardware.

test.name: parse_args_valid_positional_args_populate_config
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with a valid `<serial-device>` and `<elf-file>` and verify that the returned `AppConfig` carries the correct device path and ELF path.

test.name: parse_args_unrecognised_flag_exits_1
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with an unrecognised flag and assert that the process exits with status 1 and that a usage message is present on `stderr`.

test.name: parse_args_default_port_baud_load_when_not_supplied
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with only the two mandatory positional arguments and verify that `cfg.gdb_port == 1234`, `cfg.baud_rate == 115200`, and `cfg.load_flash == false`.

test.name: parse_args_missing_serial_device_exits_1
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with no positional arguments and assert that the process exits with status 1 and emits a usage message.

test.name: parse_args_missing_elf_file_exits_1
test.purpose: Call `parse_args()` with only `<serial-device>` and no `<elf-file>` and assert that the process exits with status 1.

test.name: main_updi_open_failure_releases_resources_and_returns_1
test.purpose: Inject a mock `updi_open()` that returns -1 and verify that `main()` does not call `rsp_listen()`, releases any already-opened resources, and returns exit code 1.

test.name: main_rsp_listen_failure_closes_updi_and_returns_1
test.purpose: Inject a mock `rsp_listen()` that returns -1 and verify that `main()` calls `updi_close()` before returning exit code 1.

test.name: main_load_flag_writes_all_pt_load_segments_to_flash
test.purpose: With `cfg.load = true` and a mock ELF context containing two `PT_LOAD` segments, verify that `main()` calls `updi_nvm_write_flash()` exactly twice, once per segment, before entering `event_loop()`.

test.name: main_load_nvm_write_failure_prints_error_and_returns_1
test.purpose: With `cfg.load = true` and a mock `updi_nvm_write_flash()` that returns -1, verify that `main()` prints an error to `stderr` and returns exit code 1 without entering `event_loop()`.

test.name: event_loop_uses_single_select_no_pthread_create
test.purpose: Instrument `event_loop()` with mock file descriptors and verify that `select()` is called with all three fds (`listen_fd`, `gdb_fd`, `updi_fd`) in the read set, and that no calls to `pthread_create()` occur.

test.name: event_loop_accepts_gdb_client_when_gdb_fd_is_minus1
test.purpose: With `cfg.gdb_fd == -1` and `listen_fd` readable, verify that `event_loop()` calls `accept()` and updates `cfg.gdb_fd`.

test.name: sigint_handler_sets_g_quit_to_1
test.purpose: Send SIGINT to the test process and verify that the signal handler installed by `main()` sets `g_quit` to 1 without performing any other operation.

test.name: event_loop_exits_immediately_when_g_quit_is_1
test.purpose: Set `g_quit = 1` before calling `event_loop()` and verify that the function returns immediately without calling `select()`.

test.name: main_cleanup_closes_gdb_elf_updi_in_order
test.purpose: On a simulated clean shutdown, verify that `main()` calls `rsp_close(gdb_fd)`, `rsp_close(listen_fd)`, `elf_close()`, and `updi_close()` in that exact order, and returns exit code 0.

file.header: Unit tests for `src/updi.c`: UART configuration, BREAK/SYNCH/LDCS link initialisation, three-frame block memory read/write, NVM flash programming, execution-control stubs, and console polling. A loopback PTY pair substitutes for real UART hardware; a `--wrap=select` linker shim lets tests inject `select()` timeouts.

test.name: updi_open_sets_8e2_raw_half_duplex_via_termios
test.purpose: Open a PTY pair, call `updi_open()` on the slave side, and inspect the resulting `termios` structure to confirm `CS8`, `CSTOPB` (2 stop bits), even-parity intent (`PARODD` clear), and raw mode (no `ICANON`/`ECHO`/`ISIG`/`OPOST`). PARENB itself is not asserted because Linux PTYs strip parity on slave reopen; parity is verified on real serial hardware in Phase 3 integration.

test.name: updi_open_returns_minus1_on_device_open_failure
test.purpose: Call `updi_open()` with a path that does not exist and verify the return value is -1.

test.name: updi_open_asserts_wake_byte_then_stcs_ctrlb
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_open()` transmits a single 0x00 wake byte first, then the STCS CTRLB frame (SYNCH `0x55`, opcode `0xC0|ASI_CTRLB = 0xC3`, value `ASI_CTRLB_CCDETDIS = 0x08`) — the first half of the avrdude-matching cold-start sequence (issue #19).

test.name: updi_open_issues_stcs_ctrla_and_ldcs_statusa
test.purpose: Verify that after STCS CTRLB the SUT writes STCS CTRLA (`0xC2`, value `ASI_CTRLA_IBDLY = 0x80`) and then probes the link with LDCS STATUSA (`0x80|ASI_STATUSA = 0x80`) — the second half of the cold-start sequence (issue #19).

test.name: updi_open_restores_session_baud_after_break
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_open()` leaves the configured session baud rate (B115200) in effect after a successful cold-start sequence — i.e. it does not corrupt the termios baud setting. The PTY responder also feeds the 32-byte SIB payload (`SYNCH`+`0xE6` → `" AVR P:2D:1-3M2 (A7.KV001.0)\0"`), so a successful run additionally exercises the SIB-read SLEEP-wake step that `updi_open()` issues after the LDCS ASI_STATUSA link probe.

test.name: updi_open_retries_cold_start_3_times_on_no_ack
test.purpose: Simulate a target that never responds and verify that `updi_open()` runs all three cold-start attempts before giving up: attempt 0 emits 1× 0x00 wake byte then STCS+STCS+LDCS at session baud; attempts 1 and 2 each emit 2× 0x00 BREAK bytes (at 300 baud via `tcsetattr`) then STCS+STCS+LDCS at session baud. With no 0x00 byte present anywhere else in the frames, this yields 1 + 2 + 2 = 5 zero bytes on the wire.

test.name: updi_open_returns_minus1_after_3_consecutive_link_failures
test.purpose: After 3 failed cold-start attempts (wake + STCS CTRLB + STCS CTRLA + LDCS STATUSA) with no response, verify that `updi_open()` returns -1.

test.name: updi_mem_read_splits_request_larger_than_256_bytes
test.purpose: Request a read of 512 bytes and verify that `updi_mem_read()` issues two consecutive 256-byte three-frame bursts rather than a single oversized transfer.

test.name: updi_mem_read_uses_repeat_ld_auto_increment_sequence
test.purpose: Capture the bytes written to the UART and verify the three-frame burst: byte 0 = `ST_PTR_WORD` (`0x69`), bytes 1–2 = address little-endian, frame 2 = `REPEAT` (`0xA0`) + count, frame 3 = `LD ptr++` (`0x24`).

test.name: updi_mem_read_uses_24bit_addressing_above_64kib
test.purpose: Request a read at address `0x012345` (above the 64 KiB boundary) and verify that `updi_mem_read()` emits the 24-bit pointer-set frame: `SYNCH`, `ST_PTR_LONG` (`0x6A`), then the address bytes in little-endian order (`0x45`, `0x23`, `0x01`), followed by the standard `REPEAT` + `LD ptr++` frames. Confirms automatic selection of the 24-bit form for AVR128DA/DB mapped-Flash access above 64 KiB.

test.name: updi_mem_read_calls_select_with_100ms_timeout_before_read
test.purpose: Using a `--wrap=select` shim that records the `timeval` argument, verify that `updi_mem_read()` passes a `timeval` of 0 seconds and 100,000 microseconds before every `read()` call.

test.name: updi_mem_read_returns_minus1_on_select_timeout
test.purpose: Inject a wrapped `select()` that returns 0 (timeout) and verify that `updi_mem_read()` immediately returns -1 without calling `read()`.

test.name: updi_mem_write_returns_0_on_success
test.purpose: Call `updi_mem_write()` targeting an SRAM address with a loopback PTY that echoes the expected ACK and verify the return value is 0.

test.name: updi_mem_write_returns_minus1_on_updi_nak
test.purpose: Inject a responder that returns a non-ACK byte instead of `UPDI_ACK` (0x40) and verify that `updi_mem_write()` returns -1.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_flash_rejects_unaligned_address
test.purpose: Call `updi_nvm_write_flash()` with a `word_addr` that is not a multiple of 512 and verify the function returns -1 without issuing any UART traffic.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_flash_rejects_non_multiple_of_512_length
test.purpose: Call `updi_nvm_write_flash()` with a `len` that is not a non-zero multiple of 512 and verify the function returns -1.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_flash_nvmprog_poll_timeout_returns_minus1
test.purpose: Inject a mock target that never sets the NVMPROG bit (`ASI_SYS_STATUS` bit 3) and verify that `updi_nvm_write_flash()` returns -1 after 100 polling iterations.

test.name: updi_nvm_write_flash_per_page_busy_timeout_returns_minus1
test.purpose: Inject a mock target that never clears `NVMCTRL_STATUS` BUSY (bit 0) after a page write and verify that `updi_nvm_write_flash()` returns -1 after 20 polling iterations.

test.name: updi_halt_returns_minus1_stub_until_ocd_layer
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_halt()` returns -1 with no UART traffic in Phase 2 — it is a stub pending the Phase 3 OCD layer.

test.name: updi_step_returns_minus1_stub_until_ocd_layer
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_step()` returns -1 with no UART traffic in Phase 2 — it is a stub pending the Phase 3 OCD layer.

test.name: updi_run_returns_minus1_stub_until_ocd_layer
test.purpose: Verify that `updi_run()` returns -1 with no UART traffic in Phase 2 — it is a stub pending the Phase 3 OCD layer.

test.name: updi_console_poll_returns_pending_bytes_without_halting
test.purpose: Pre-stuff the master end of the PTY with 4 bytes and verify that `updi_console_poll()` returns 4 and copies the bytes to the output buffer without calling `updi_halt()`.

test.name: updi_console_poll_returns_0_when_output_buffer_empty
test.purpose: With no data pending on the master end, verify that `updi_console_poll()` returns 0 in a non-blocking manner.

file.header: Unit tests for `src/gdb_rsp.c`: socket configuration, RSP packet framing, register and memory handlers, breakpoint management, session lifecycle packets, and monitor relay. Uses a `socketpair()` as a drop-in socket substitute so all tests run without a real GDB client.

test.name: rsp_listen_sets_so_reuseaddr_before_bind
test.purpose: Verify that `rsp_listen()` calls `setsockopt()` with `SO_REUSEADDR` enabled before calling `bind()`.

test.name: rsp_accept_sets_tcp_nodelay_on_client_socket
test.purpose: After `rsp_accept()` returns a client socket, verify that `TCP_NODELAY` has been set on that socket via `getsockopt()`.

test.name: rsp_recv_packet_discards_leading_ack_nak_bytes
test.purpose: Feed a byte stream that begins with `+` and `-` characters before the `$` delimiter and verify that `rsp_recv_packet()` discards them and correctly decodes the payload that follows.

test.name: rsp_recv_packet_sends_plus_on_valid_checksum
test.purpose: Feed a well-formed RSP packet with a correct XOR checksum and verify that `rsp_recv_packet()` writes `+` to the socket and returns the payload length.

test.name: rsp_recv_packet_sends_minus_and_returns_minus1_on_bad_checksum
test.purpose: Feed an RSP packet with a deliberately corrupted checksum and verify that `rsp_recv_packet()` writes `-` to the socket and returns -1.

test.name: on_read_regs_g_returns_78_char_hex_string
test.purpose: Invoke the `g` packet handler via `rsp_dispatch()` and verify that the RSP reply payload is exactly 78 hex characters, representing all 36 GDB AVR register values.

test.name: on_read_regs_g_places_pc_little_endian_at_positions_70_77
test.purpose: Inject a known PC value via the mock UPDI and verify that hex characters at positions 70–77 of the `g` reply encode the PC as 4-byte little-endian.

test.name: on_write_regs_G_writes_all_registers_via_updi_mem_write
test.purpose: Dispatch a `G` packet containing 78 hex characters and verify that the handler calls `updi_mem_write()` with the decoded register values and returns `OK`.

test.name: on_write_regs_P_writes_single_register_via_updi_mem_write
test.purpose: Dispatch a `P` packet specifying register index 5 and a new value, and verify that the handler calls `updi_mem_write()` targeting only the R5 SRAM address and returns `OK`.

test.name: on_read_mem_m_calls_updi_mem_read_and_returns_hex
test.purpose: Dispatch an `m addr,4` packet for a SRAM address and verify that the handler calls `updi_mem_read()` with the decoded address and length and returns an 8-character hex string.

test.name: on_write_mem_M_calls_updi_mem_write_for_sram_address
test.purpose: Dispatch an `M addr,4:data` packet targeting a SRAM address and verify that the handler calls `updi_mem_write()` and returns `OK`.

test.name: on_write_mem_X_calls_nvm_write_flash_for_flash_address
test.purpose: Dispatch an `X addr,2:data` packet targeting a FLASH address and verify that the handler calls `updi_nvm_write_flash()` and returns `OK`.

test.name: on_insert_bp_writes_break_opcode_and_saves_original_word
test.purpose: Dispatch a `Z0 addr,2` packet and verify that the handler reads and saves the original 2-byte instruction word, writes the AVR BREAK opcode (0x9598) via `updi_nvm_write_flash()`, and returns `OK`.

test.name: on_insert_bp_duplicate_returns_ok_without_reflash
test.purpose: Dispatch the same `Z0 addr,2` breakpoint insert twice and verify that `updi_nvm_write_flash()` is called only once, and that the second call returns `OK` immediately.

test.name: on_remove_bp_restores_saved_instruction_word
test.purpose: After inserting a breakpoint with `Z0`, dispatch `z0` for the same address and verify that `updi_nvm_write_flash()` is called with the original saved instruction word.

test.name: on_remove_bp_unknown_address_returns_error_reply
test.purpose: Dispatch `z0` for an address that has no entry in the breakpoint table and verify that the handler returns a GDB error reply.

test.name: on_insert_bp_returns_E08_when_table_full
test.purpose: Fill all `RSP_MAX_BREAKPOINTS` (16) breakpoint table slots with distinct addresses, then dispatch one more `Z0` insert and verify the response is `E08`.

test.name: on_step_s_calls_updi_step_and_sends_T05_stop_reason
test.purpose: Dispatch an `s` packet and verify that the handler calls `updi_step()` once and sends a stop-reason reply of the form `T05thread:<id>;`.

test.name: on_continue_calls_updi_run_then_fsm_invalidate
test.purpose: Dispatch a `c` packet and verify that the handler calls `updi_run()` and then `fsm_invalidate()` in that order before polling for a halt.

test.name: on_continue_rebuilds_thread_list_after_halt_and_sends_stop
test.purpose: After the simulated halt triggered by `on_continue`, verify that `fsm_build_thread_list()` is called and the handler sends a stop-reason packet to the GDB client.

test.name: rsp_dispatch_qsupported_returns_feature_string_no_target_access
test.purpose: Dispatch a `qSupported` packet and verify that a non-empty feature string is returned and that no UPDI calls are made.

test.name: rsp_dispatch_qattached_returns_1_no_target_access
test.purpose: Dispatch a `qAttached` packet and verify the reply is `1` and that no UPDI calls are made.

test.name: on_detach_D_resumes_target_closes_socket_resets_gdb_fd
test.purpose: Dispatch a `D` packet and verify that the handler calls `updi_run()`, closes the GDB client socket, and sets `cfg->gdb_fd` to -1 without exiting the server process.

test.name: on_kill_k_sets_g_quit_to_1
test.purpose: Dispatch a `k` packet and verify that `g_quit` is set to 1, causing the event loop to exit on its next iteration.

test.name: on_monitor_qRcmd_passes_hex_body_to_monitor_dispatch
test.purpose: Dispatch a `qRcmd` packet with a hex-encoded command body and verify that `monitor_dispatch()` receives the same hex-encoded string without any pre-decoding.

test.name: on_monitor_returns_ok_when_monitor_dispatch_succeeds
test.purpose: Inject a mock `monitor_dispatch()` that returns 0 and verify that the `qRcmd` handler sends `OK` to the GDB client.

test.name: on_monitor_sends_o_packet_error_on_updi_failure
test.purpose: Inject a mock `monitor_dispatch()` that returns -1 and verify that the `qRcmd` handler sends an O-packet error message to the GDB console.

test.name: H_packet_stores_thread_id_for_register_operations
test.purpose: Dispatch `Hg3` (set thread 3 for register operations) and then a `g` packet, and verify that `fsm_get_registers()` is called with the thread entry for GDB thread ID 3.

test.name: H_packet_minus1_and_0_both_map_to_active_fsm_thread
test.purpose: Dispatch `Hg-1` and `Hg0` in turn, each followed by a `g` packet, and verify that both select the active FSM thread's register frame.

file.header: Unit tests for `src/elf_parser.c`: ELF validation, symbol table loading, avrOS sentinel symbol discovery, Harvard address conversion, fail-safe degradation, and context cleanup. Fixture ELF binaries are generated by a helper script in `tests/fixtures/`.

test.name: elf_open_accepts_valid_avr_elf32_binary
test.purpose: Call `elf_open()` with a well-formed AVR ELF32 fixture file and verify the return value is non-negative and `ctx.sym_count > 0`.

test.name: elf_open_returns_minus1_on_invalid_elf_magic
test.purpose: Call `elf_open()` with a file whose first 4 bytes are not the ELF magic sequence and verify the return value is -1.

test.name: elf_open_returns_minus1_on_wrong_machine_type
test.purpose: Call `elf_open()` with a valid ELF32 file that has `e_machine != EM_AVR` and verify the return value is -1.

test.name: elf_open_loads_symtab_and_strtab_into_heap_buffers
test.purpose: After a successful `elf_open()`, verify that `ctx.symtab` and `ctx.strtab` are non-NULL heap pointers, and that `ctx.sym_count` and `ctx.strtab_size` reflect the actual section sizes.

test.name: elf_open_frees_partial_allocs_and_returns_minus1_on_malloc_failure
test.purpose: Inject a mock `malloc()` that fails on the second allocation, call `elf_open()`, and verify the return value is -1 and no heap memory remains allocated.

test.name: elf_find_avros_tables_performs_single_linear_scan
test.purpose: Instrument `elf_find_avros_tables()` with a mock symbol table and verify that each symbol entry is examined at most once regardless of how many avrOS sentinels are present.

test.name: elf_find_avros_tables_populates_all_7_avros_sentinel_fields
test.purpose: Call `elf_find_avros_tables()` with a fixture ELF that contains all 7 avrOS sentinel symbols (`__start_FSM_TABLE`, `__stop_FSM_TABLE`, `__start_QUE_TABLE`, `__stop_QUE_TABLE`, `__start_EVNT_TABLE`, `__stop_EVNT_TABLE`, `currStateMachine`) and verify every populated field of `AvrOsSymbolIndex` is non-zero.

test.name: elf_flash_addr_applies_vma_minus_base_over_2_formula
test.purpose: Call `elf_flash_addr()` with known `vma` and `ctx.flash_base` values and verify the return equals `(vma - flash_base) / 2`.

test.name: elf_flash_addr_all_avros_symbol_addresses_use_word_formula
test.purpose: After `elf_find_avros_tables()`, verify that every FLASH-resident address stored in `AvrOsSymbolIndex` was computed via `elf_flash_addr()`, not as a raw VMA.

test.name: elf_find_avros_tables_returns_0_on_partial_symbol_match
test.purpose: Call `elf_find_avros_tables()` with a fixture ELF containing only 4 of the 8 avrOS sentinels and verify the return value is 0 (not -1).

test.name: elf_find_avros_tables_zero_initialises_absent_symbol_fields
test.purpose: After `elf_find_avros_tables()` on a partial-symbol ELF, verify that each field in `AvrOsSymbolIndex` that corresponds to a missing symbol is zero.

test.name: elf_close_frees_symtab_strtab_and_closes_fd
test.purpose: After a successful `elf_open()`, call `elf_close()` and verify that the file descriptor is closed and no memory is leaked (checked via Valgrind or AddressSanitizer).

test.name: elf_close_safe_on_partially_initialised_context
test.purpose: Construct an `ElfContext` with `symtab = NULL`, `strtab` allocated, and `fd = -1`, call `elf_close()`, and verify no crash or double-free occurs.

test.name: elf_open_sets_flash_base_and_sram_base_from_pt_load_segments
test.purpose: After a successful `elf_open()` on the full fixture, verify that `ctx.flash_base` equals the VMA of the first `PT_LOAD` segment (0x00000000 for the fixture) and `ctx.sram_base` equals the VMA of the second `PT_LOAD` segment (0x00804000 for the AVR128DA28 fixture).

file.header: Unit tests for `src/fsm_mapper.c`: FSM table reading, stable GDB thread ID assignment, active-thread identification, g-packet register frame construction, thread count capping, and stack-free guarantees. All UPDI calls are stubbed via a mock layer.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_reads_fsm_table_from_flash_via_updi
test.purpose: Verify that `fsm_build_thread_list()` calls `updi_mem_read()` targeting `idx->fsm_table_addr` and reads `idx->fsm_table_count` consecutive 9-byte `fsmStateMachineDescr_t` records.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_returns_minus1_on_updi_failure
test.purpose: Inject a mock `updi_mem_read()` that returns -1 and verify that `fsm_build_thread_list()` propagates the error by returning -1.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_assigns_1_based_thread_ids_in_order
test.purpose: Build a thread list from 3 FSM entries and verify that the resulting `gdb_id` values are 1, 2, and 3, in the order the entries appear in the FLASH table.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_thread_ids_stable_across_calls
test.purpose: Call `fsm_build_thread_list()` twice with the same FSM table content and verify that each FSM entry maps to the same `gdb_id` on both calls.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_sets_active_thread_from_current_fsm_ptr
test.purpose: Inject a mock `currStateMachine` SRAM value matching the second FSM entry's `stateMachine` pointer and verify that only that entry has `is_active == true` and `ctx->active_id == 2`.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_sets_active_id_0_when_no_entry_matches
test.purpose: Inject a `current_fsm` SRAM value that does not match any registered FSM and verify that `ctx->active_id == 0`.

test.name: fsm_get_registers_places_state_fn_as_pc_at_hex_positions_70_77
test.purpose: Call `fsm_get_registers()` for a thread whose `state_fn = 0xABCD` and verify that the 78-character g-packet buffer contains the little-endian encoding of 0xABCD at hex character positions 70–77.

test.name: fsm_get_registers_non_active_r0_r31_sreg_spl_sph_all_zero
test.purpose: Call `fsm_get_registers()` for a non-active thread and verify that hex positions 0–69 of the 78-character buffer are all `'0'`.

test.name: fsm_get_registers_active_thread_reads_live_sreg_spl_sph
test.purpose: Call `fsm_get_registers()` for the active thread with a mock that returns known SREG, SPL, and SPH values, and verify they appear at hex positions 64–65, 66–67, and 68–69 respectively.

test.name: fsm_build_thread_list_caps_at_32_entries_and_logs_warning
test.purpose: Inject an FSM table with 33 entries and verify that `fsm_build_thread_list()` returns `FSM_MAX_THREADS` (32) and emits a diagnostic warning without returning an error.

test.name: fsm_get_registers_non_active_no_updi_read_of_stack
test.purpose: Call `fsm_get_registers()` for a non-active thread and verify that `updi_mem_read()` is never called with any stack-region address.

file.header: Unit tests for `src/monitor.c`: hex command decoding, prefix matching, per-sub-command UPDI reads, O-packet output formatting, 512-byte buffer constraint, and the no-halt guarantee. All UPDI calls are intercepted by a mock layer that records calls and returns injected data.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_hex_decodes_cmd_before_prefix_matching
test.purpose: Pass `monitor_dispatch()` a hex-encoded `"avros events"` command and verify the function routes to `cmd_events()`, confirming that decoding occurs before prefix matching.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_treats_invalid_hex_sequence_as_unrecognised
test.purpose: Pass `monitor_dispatch()` an odd-length hex string and verify it returns -2 without crashing or producing partial output.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_rejects_cmd_without_avros_space_prefix
test.purpose: Pass a hex-encoded command that decodes to `"other events"` and verify `monitor_dispatch()` returns -2.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_sends_usage_hint_o_packet_on_bad_prefix
test.purpose: Pass a command with an unrecognised prefix and verify that `monitor_dispatch()` sends at least one RSP O-packet containing a usage-hint string before returning -2.

test.name: cmd_events_reads_event_count_descriptors_from_evnt_table
test.purpose: Dispatch `"avros events"` and verify that `updi_mem_read()` is called with address `idx->event_table_addr` and a length equal to `idx->event_count` × 4 bytes (`evntDescriptor_t` size).

test.name: cmd_events_reports_name_and_status_value_per_descriptor
test.purpose: Inject two `evntDescriptor_t` records pointing at FLASH names `"RX"`, `"TX"` and 1-byte SRAM status values `0x01`, `0x00` and verify the decoded O-packet text contains both names and both status bytes formatted as `0xXX`.

test.name: cmd_events_output_is_hex_encoded_o_packet
test.purpose: Dispatch `"avros events"` and verify the single captured `rsp_send_packet()` payload begins with `'O'` and every subsequent character is an uppercase hex digit (`[0-9A-F]`), with an overall odd length.

test.name: cmd_queues_reads_queue_count_descriptors_from_que_table
test.purpose: Dispatch `"avros queues"` and verify that `updi_mem_read()` is called with `idx->queue_table_addr` and a length equal to `idx->queue_count` × 10 bytes (`queDescriptor_t` size).

test.name: cmd_queues_formats_capacity_and_sizeofelement_for_each_entry
test.purpose: Inject two `queDescriptor_t` records with `(capacity, sizeOfElement)` of `(8, 1)` and `(16, 4)` respectively and verify the decoded O-packet text contains `"capacity=8 sizeOfElement=1"` and `"capacity=16 sizeOfElement=4"`.

test.name: monitor_dispatch_and_helpers_never_call_updi_halt
test.purpose: Execute both sub-commands (`events`, `queues`) through `monitor_dispatch()` and verify that `updi_halt()` is never called by inspecting the mock call log.

file.header: Integration tests validating system-level properties not covered by per-LLR unit tests: server startup latency (HLR-005), RSP protocol purity (HLR-020), and build portability (HLR-033, HLR-034).

test.name: integration_server_ready_within_2_seconds_of_client_connect
test.purpose: Launch `avr-updi-gdb` against a loopback UPDI stub and a fixture ELF, connect a GDB client, and measure the elapsed time from TCP accept to the first valid RSP response. Assert the elapsed time is less than 2.0 seconds.

test.name: integration_server_emits_only_standard_rsp_no_ide_extensions
test.purpose: Capture all TCP traffic from a full debug session (connect, register read, memory read, continue, breakpoint, detach) and verify that every server-originated packet conforms to the GDB RSP specification with no DAP, Cortex-Debug, or other IDE-specific packet types present.

test.name: build_compiles_clean_on_linux_with_c99_and_posix
test.purpose: Execute `make` with `CC=gcc CFLAGS="-std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -D_POSIX_C_SOURCE=200809L"` and assert that the build exits with status 0 and produces no compiler warnings or errors on a Linux x86-64 host.

test.name: runtime_links_only_libc_no_heavyweight_deps
test.purpose: Run `ldd avr-updi-gdb` on the linked binary and verify that the only shared-library dependency is `libc.so`. Assert that no Java runtime, Python interpreter, Electron libraries, or other non-POSIX dependencies appear.

file.header: Verification tests for the Makefile install/uninstall targets, the `check-tools` pre-flight target, and the Unix man page. Tests fork a subprocess or invoke `make` directly and inspect the resulting file-system state or exit codes.

test.name: check_tools_exits_nonzero_when_required_tool_is_absent
test.purpose: Temporarily shadow a required tool (e.g. `avr-gcc`) with a dummy wrapper that is not executable, then run `make check-tools` and verify it exits with a non-zero status and prints a diagnostic to stderr naming the missing tool.

test.name: make_install_places_binary_at_prefix_bin
test.purpose: Run `make install PREFIX=/tmp/aod_test_$$` (using a temporary directory as the prefix) and verify that the file `$(PREFIX)/bin/avr-updi-gdb` exists and is executable after the target completes.

test.name: make_install_places_man_page_at_prefix_man1
test.purpose: After `make install PREFIX=...`, verify that the file `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1/avr-updi-gdb.1` exists and that `man -l` parses it without error.

test.name: make_uninstall_removes_all_installed_files
test.purpose: After `make install PREFIX=...`, run `make uninstall PREFIX=...` and verify that both `$(PREFIX)/bin/avr-updi-gdb` and `$(PREFIX)/share/man/man1/avr-updi-gdb.1` no longer exist.

test.name: user_manual_exists_and_contains_required_sections
test.purpose: Read `doc/UserManual.md` and verify the file exists and contains all required section headings: Prerequisites, Build, Connection Wiring, Usage (or Options), and at least one Example.

test.name: make_bundle_produces_deb_package
test.purpose: Run `make bundle VERSION=0.1.0` and verify that `dist/avr-updi-gdb_0.1.0_amd64.deb` exists, that `dpkg-deb --info` exits 0, and that `dpkg-deb --contents` lists both `./usr/bin/avr-updi-gdb` and `./usr/share/man/man1/avr-updi-gdb.1`.

test.name: make_bundle_produces_rpm_package
test.purpose: Run `make bundle VERSION=0.1.0` and verify that `dist/avr-updi-gdb-0.1.0-1.x86_64.rpm` exists and that `rpm -qp --list` exits 0 and lists both `/usr/bin/avr-updi-gdb` and `/usr/share/man/man1/avr-updi-gdb.1`.

test.name: make_bundle_produces_homebrew_formula
test.purpose: Run `make bundle VERSION=0.1.0` and verify that `dist/avr-updi-gdb.rb` exists, is valid Ruby syntax (parseable by `ruby -c`), and contains the required fields: `desc`, `url`, `sha256`, `version`, and an `install` block.

file.header: Unit and harness-level tests covering the `--device` one-shot diagnostic mode: argument parsing, mutual exclusion with `--load`, `updi_read_device_info()` success and failure paths over a PTY, the human-readable report format, and verification that the diagnostic path bypasses the GDB listener.

test.name: parse_args_accepts_device_flag_without_elf_operand
test.purpose: Invoke `parse_args()` with `argv = {"avr-updi-gdb", "--device", "/dev/ttyUSB0"}` and assert `cfg.device_info == true`, `cfg.serial_device == "/dev/ttyUSB0"`, `cfg.elf_path == NULL`, and `parse_args()` returns without exiting.

test.name: parse_args_rejects_device_combined_with_load
test.purpose: Fork a subprocess that calls `parse_args()` with `--device --load /dev/ttyUSB0 fw.elf`; assert the child exits with status 1 and that captured stderr contains `"--device is mutually exclusive with --load"`.

test.name: updi_read_device_info_returns_sigrow_and_asi_bytes
test.purpose: Open a PTY pair; in a helper thread script the slave end to echo half-duplex bytes and respond to a SIGROW DEVICEID read at `0x1100`-`0x1102` with canned signature `0x1E 0x97 0x0A`, a SYSCFG.REVID read at `0x0F01` returning `0xA6`, a SIGROW.SERNUM read at `0x1110`-`0x111F` returning a canned 16-byte serial number, and to LDCS reads of SYS_STATUS / KEY_STATUS / STATUSB. Call `updi_read_device_info()` and assert all struct fields match the canned values and that the function returns 0 with `info.fail_op == NULL`.

test.name: updi_read_device_info_reports_failed_step_on_nak
test.purpose: Drive the PTY harness to return an unexpected byte in place of the SIGROW response. Assert `updi_read_device_info()` returns -1, `info.fail_op` equals the string `"sigrow"`, and `info.fail_errno` is negative.

test.name: run_device_mode_prints_report_to_stdout
test.purpose: Capture `stdout` from `run_device_mode()` driven by the PTY harness with signature `0x1E 0x97 0x0A`. Assert the captured output contains the literal lines `Serial device:`, `Baud rate:`, `Signature:`, `Family:`, `Revision:`, `Serial:`, and `UPDI status:` (case-sensitive prefix match).

test.name: device_mode_does_not_call_rsp_listen
test.purpose: Link the test binary with a stub `rsp_listen()` that flags a global. Invoke `run_device_mode()` to completion and assert the flag remains clear, proving the diagnostic path bypasses GDB listener startup.

file.header: On-target hardware integration test harness for the AVR-Dx UPDI driver, device-info report, SRAM/FLASH memory access, and the GDB RSP server. Manual-only: never invoked by `make test`. Driven by the Makefile targets `hw-test`, `hw-test-nvm`, `hw-test-rsp`, and `hw-test-all`. Configurable via `HW_PORT`, `HW_DEVICE_ID`, `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR`, `HW_RSP_PORT`, `HW_TEST_ELF`, `HW_ADDR_24BIT`, `HW_VERBOSE` (env or CLI). Destructive groups gated by `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES` (FLASH) and `HW_TEST_RSP=YES` (RSP).

test.name: A1_port_open_and_cold_start_handshake
test.purpose: Open the configured serial device and execute the UPDI cold-start handshake (BREAK + SYNCH). Assert that `updi_open()` returns a valid file descriptor and that the handshake completes without error. Implicitly verifies that `HW_PORT` / `--port` resolution and CLI-overrides-environment precedence work end-to-end.

test.name: A2_read_device_info
test.purpose: Call `updi_read_device_info()` against the live target and capture the returned struct. Assert the call returns 0 and `info.fail_op == NULL`; the captured fields are reused by A3..A7.

test.name: A3_deviceid_matches_expected
test.purpose: Compare the SIGROW `DEVICEID0..2` bytes against the configured `HW_DEVICE_ID` (default `0x1E970A`). Assert exact byte-for-byte match.

test.name: A4_signature_non_zero_non_ff
test.purpose: Assert that the captured SIGROW signature is neither all `0x00` nor all `0xFF` (catches dead-bus / pull-up-only conditions that A3 might miss if `HW_DEVICE_ID` were misconfigured).

test.name: A5_revid_non_zero
test.purpose: Assert that the captured `SYSCFG.REVID` byte is non-zero.

test.name: A6_sernum_non_zero_non_ff
test.purpose: Assert that the 10-byte SIGROW `SERNUM` field is neither all `0x00` nor all `0xFF`.

test.name: A7_nvmprog_bit_clear
test.purpose: Assert that the `ASI_SYS_STATUS.NVMPROG` bit is clear, proving the target is not stuck in a programming session at harness start-up.

test.name: B0_sram_single_byte_round_trip
test.purpose: Write one byte to `HW_SRAM_ADDR` via `updi_mem_write()`, read it back via `updi_mem_read()`, and assert byte-equality. Reaching this test through any of the four `hw-test*` Makefile targets implicitly verifies that the recipes forward `HW_PORT`, `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, and related variables to the child process.

test.name: B1_sram_64_byte_round_trip
test.purpose: Write a 64-byte deterministic pattern to `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, read it back, and assert byte-for-byte match.

test.name: B1a_sigrow_read_repeatability
test.purpose: Read SIGROW twice via `updi_mem_read()` and assert both reads return identical bytes. Isolates the read path from the write path; a failure indicates a bus or framing problem rather than RAM corruption.

test.name: B1b_sram_constant_0xAA_round_trip
test.purpose: Write 64 bytes of constant `0xAA` to `HW_SRAM_ADDR` and read back. Asserts that data fidelity does not depend on byte value (rules out value-dependent framing or escape-byte bugs).

test.name: B1c_sram_write_once_read_twice
test.purpose: Write a known pattern to `HW_SRAM_ADDR` once, then read the region back twice; assert both reads are identical. On failure, the harness shall print a hint instructing the operator to choose a different `--sram-addr` / `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, because the live target CPU is writing to the probed region.

test.name: B2_sram_600_byte_round_trip
test.purpose: Write a 600-byte buffer to `HW_SRAM_ADDR`, read it back, and assert byte-equality. Exercises multi-chunk transfer and any internal block-size boundary handling in the UPDI driver.

test.name: B3_flash_24bit_addressing_smoke
test.purpose: When `HW_ADDR_24BIT` is true, perform a small read at `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR` using the UPDI 24-bit addressing path; assert the call returns the expected number of bytes. Skipped when `HW_ADDR_24BIT` is false.

test.name: C1_flash_erase_and_write
test.purpose: When `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES`, erase the FLASH page at `HW_FLASH_PAGE_ADDR` and write a deterministic pattern via the NVM controller; assert all NVM controller status checks succeed. Skipped otherwise.

test.name: C2_flash_read_back_verify
test.purpose: Read the FLASH page written by C1 and assert a byte-for-byte match against the written pattern. Skipped unless `HW_TEST_NVM_CONFIRM=YES`.

test.name: D1_rsp_server_accepts_tcp_connection
test.purpose: When `HW_TEST_RSP=YES`, `fork`+`execl` the production `build/avr-updi-gdb` against the configured serial port; open a TCP client to `127.0.0.1:HW_RSP_PORT` and assert the connect succeeds within a bounded timeout. Skipped otherwise.

test.name: D2_rsp_qsupported_round_trip
test.purpose: Send an RSP `$qSupported#37` packet to the spawned server and assert a non-empty, properly-framed RSP reply is received. Skipped unless `HW_TEST_RSP=YES`. On completion the harness shall terminate the spawned server cleanly via SIGTERM + `waitpid`.
